howTo: Add linear dimensions to the chain. For each feature, specify its nominal length, upper deviation, and lower deviation in the same unit.
Assign the direction of each dimension in the stack: positive (+1) for additive features or negative (-1) for internal gaps, subtractive steps, or pockets.
Evaluate both the deterministic Worst-Case (WC) boundary interval for guaranteed fit and the Root-Sum-Square (RSS) statistical interval for high-volume production sizing.
formula: X_nom = Σ (dir_i · N_i) | WC_max = Σ max(dir_i · [N_i + dev]) | WC_min = Σ min(dir_i · [N_i + dev]) | T_rss = √(Σ t_i²)

examples.title: Two-part additive assembly stack
examples.description: Two pinned plates stacked end-to-end: Part A is 20 ± 0.10 mm and Part B is 10 ± 0.05 mm.
notes: Worst-case limits guarantee zero interference across 100% of manufactured parts regardless of supplier process capability.
Sensitivity analysis shows Part A contributes 80% of the total variance due to its larger ±0.10 mm tolerance band.

examples.title: Shaft and bushing internal axial clearance
examples.description: Shaft shoulder (50 ± 0.20 mm) fitting inside a housing cavity (40 ± 0.10 mm) to verify axial end-play.
notes: The subtractive feature reverses its upper and lower bounds: minimum clearance occurs when housing is at lower limit (49.8 mm) and shaft is at upper limit (40.1 mm), resulting in 9.7 mm.
Always verify that minimum clearance remains strictly positive to prevent binding under thermal expansion.

commonMistakes: Entering lower deviation as a positive magnitude when it is below nominal (e.g. entering +0.1 instead of -0.1).
Applying RSS statistical stacking on low-volume production (< 30 parts) or uncentered processes where normal distribution cannot be assumed.
Neglecting thermal expansion differences between mating materials (e.g. aluminum housing with steel shaft) over the operating temperature spectrum.
assumptions: One-dimensional linear stackup: all dimensions are parallel and coplanar along a single measurement vector.
RSS statistical stacking assumes independent, normally distributed component tolerances with a process capability index Cp ≥ 1.0 centered at nominal.
Geometric form, orientation, and location tolerances (GD&T feature control frames, MMC/MMR bonus tolerances) require separate 3D variation analysis.
